inherited_trait_default_evidence.runtime_evidence: Five native comparison rows explicitly execute !=; Rust comparison_row uses left != right with matching truth values and both constness directions.
inherited_trait_default_evidence.limitation: The crate exports its generic PartialEq impl and body-bearing eq; ne is inherited from core rather than a separately implemented or normalized crate method. These two native declaration IDs are recorded separately from the19 crate-body bindings.

behavior: Same-type assignment and explicit self-assignment preserve original owner identity, index, captured end, current pointer and block-end pointer without querying or dereferencing an owner. Mutable-to-const assignment copies actual raw pointer state through existing conversion without granting writable access.

Both initialize_with specializations replace the cursor by a freshly captured index0 cursor only after checked capture succeeds. They accept a different supplied owner, switch subsequent navigation identity, and recapture the current end. Init and Initialize map to this shared behavior; no redundant spelling aliases are added.

PartialEq/Eq preserve owner-sensitive equality without imposing T:PartialEq or T:Eq. Inherited core PartialEq::ne supplies native inequality. Named less_than/greater_than/at_most/at_least preserve native cross-owner positional comparisons without imposing an invalid Rust PartialOrd law where different owners can compare equal by position.

Each relational operator uses the native subtraction direction. With signed-minimum position, minimum<zero and zero>minimum are defined and true, while the reversed signed-subtraction expressions overflow and are rejected by Rust. Native UBSan probes execute only the defined directions.

Twenty native rows establish assignment of transferred cache pointers, returned receiver identity and self assignment; matching owner/index with a different pointer; different owner with the same pointer; saved end4 against refilled size6; Init on moved-empty source; mutable/shared and const-argument legacy overload observations; recaptured end after append; and cross-owner/cross-const relational truth tables.

Seven new Rust tests cover the20-row trace, non-Clone/non-Eq payloads, default-copy clearing, both initializer specializations preserving prior state after unsupported zero-sized live-slot rejection, navigation identity after owner switch, signed-overflow direction, and pointer-free metadata assignment/comparison after allocation destruction. The final normal suite and strict Miri include all52 original native/Rust runtime names.

Nineteen exact native inventory IDs bind10 unique body-bearing Rust methods. Two additional native != IDs have separate inherited-standard-trait source/runtime evidence; no extra crate method body is fabricated for them. Global API and legacy completion credit remain unchanged.
limitations: Legacy Iterator Init/Initialize taking const NCollection_DynamicArray& permit native const_cast access. The Rust mutable specialization requires &mut DynamicArray and thus supports a narrower callable borrowing domain even where the actual C++ source object is mutable. Truly shared or const owners are not converted into writable references.

Initialization requires supported initialized slots and fitting nonzero-sized/nonzero-stride layouts. Unsupported layout errors are checked Rust extensions, not assertions of native exception/undefined behavior equivalence. Failure leaves prior cursor state untouched.

Navigation after original-owner destruction still requires an unavailable original owner reference; assignment and comparison only copy/compare metadata and never dereference the stored owner. A non-null cached pointer after payload destruction is not evidence of live storage; actual value access remains unsafe.

Native signed cast behavior is evidenced on the pinned x86_64 compiler/runtime. Overflowing signed subtraction is never run as a native oracle, and comparisons return checked Rust errors outside the native defined arithmetic domain.

The adapter does not reproduce virtual legacy Iterator More/Next subclass dispatch, arbitrary enable_if template overrides, native unrestricted const-cast mutability, zero-stride retained mutation or constructor-failure leaked resource lifetime behavior. Existing detached and standard iterator conveniences remain separately scoped.

Proof source hashes capture this branch snapshot. Adding assignment/comparison submodule declarations changes cached.rs file hash; prior receipt hashes remain historical. Shared parity and global coverage ledgers are untouched.
